critical_code_review_comments: Wlad-Style headline implementation is consistent and well-executed across 4 files (Hero/HighTicketClose/UserForm/Kurse). 14 eyebrows '▸' + 10 italic emphasis spans counted on landing alone — design rhythm holds.

Hero.jsx Bonus-Kurs section H2 (line 497) is the ONE remaining landing-section H2 that has NOT been refactored to multi-line Wlad-style. It currently reads as a single-line H2 and breaks the rhythm vs. sections 2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10.

There is no centralized umlaut-sanity lint step — strongly recommend adding a pre-commit grep guard for /ausgewahlten|Feedbackgesprach|Zunachst|\bfur\b|Fuhrung/ to prevent regressions like this slipping in on every iteration. Hero.jsx + Roadmap.jsx are recurring culprits.
Em-dash usage in pull-quote attribution is a stylistic choice but violates explicit iter34 spec; consider building an ESLint custom rule that bans U+2014 in JSX literals.

rca of the issue: Typos 'Zunachst' (Hero.jsx:451) and 'ausgewahlten' (Hero.jsx:497) are leftover ASCII-fallbacks from a previous editing pass where umlauts were stripped (possibly an encoding hiccup on copy-paste). Same root cause in Roadmap.jsx where 'fur' + 'Fuhrung' appear repeatedly. Em-dashes were missed in the / + /report attribution lines because the prior typography sweep focused on body copy but not on pull-quote attribution lines (the dashes are intentionally used as attribution markers — but spec explicitly forbids them). MITIGATION: (1) sed/perl replace umlauts in Hero.jsx + Roadmap.jsx, (2) grep -n '—' src/pages/*.jsx and convert each to '·' or '-' or '— ' → '· ', (3) add pre-commit hook to enforce no ASCII-fallback umlauts AND no em-dash in committed JSX.
